name: semaphore
algorithm: t workers (Mk: tasks; Go: goroutines; Zig: OS threads) share one counting semaphore of 4 permits; each does n rounds of acquire one permit, add one to an atomic in-use count and count a violation when it passes 4, subtract one, release. Prints t * n and the violations (0) (README.md).

skip.c: no semaphore in standard C (C11 <threads.h> has mtx_t and cnd_t only; sem_t is POSIX)
skip.rust: no semaphore in Rust's std (tokio's is a crate)
skip.mk-wrap: the only arithmetic is the counters, which stay below 2^40

models.go: goroutines (GOMAXPROCS 8), a buffered channel of capacity 4 (Go's std idiom; weight 1 only)

no_counts: B24 does not apply: the checksum, every round counted and no violation, shows that no more than 4 held a permit at once
notes: Concurrency row (B19): every column runs on logical CPUs 0, 2, ..., 14 (mask 0x5555) with 8 threads (MK_CARRIERS=8, GOMAXPROCS=8). Zig uses OS threads, labelled so.
Written by std-sync2 (status/std-sync2.md, M6 session 1); checksums from the workload's arithmetic.
